mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Certificate of Registered Matters / Company Registration Certificate)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille Convention country: original certificate issued in Korean, notarized translation, Apostille certificate issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Korea; no consular legalization. Non-member state: notarization, authentication by the issuing state's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then Korean Consular Section legalization; apostille path not available.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of Existence of Registration)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille Convention country: notarized Korean-language original, Apostille by MOFA Korea; no consular legalization. Non-member: origin-state MOFA authentication followed by Korean embassy/consulate legalization only.

Non-member state: notarization, state-level authentication, and Korean consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Incorporation (Memorandum and Articles of Association; Jeong-gwan)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille country: notarized original in Korean with English translation, Apostille by MOFA; no consular legalization. Non-member state: distinct consular legalization of the notarized instrument; apostille cannot be used.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed depository bank of the investor (e.g., Kookmin, Shinhan, or any FSS-regulated bank)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille Convention state: original on bank letterhead, notarized signature of bank officer, Apostille by the competent apostille authority; no consular legalization. Non-member state: consular legalization by Korean embassy/consulate of the notarized letter.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Investor's Certificate of Identity and Registered Address (Certificate of Personal Seal Impression / Identity Certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Local notary public, city/municipal office, or the corporate registration office of the investor's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille member origin: notarization followed by Apostille certificate from the origin country's designated competent authority, accepted directly by Korean counterparties. Non-Apostille origin: certificate must be notarized, authenticated by the origin Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then legalized by the Korean Embassy/Consulate in that jurisdiction.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all ultimate beneficial owners, directors, senior managers, authorized signatories, and counterparties against the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) watchlist, Korean Financial Services Commission (FSC) issued measures, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, US OFAC Specially Designated Nationals list, US BIS Entity List, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, and the UK Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation list. Each candidate must undergo adverse-media review, zero-tolerance hit verification, and domestic judicial/disciplinary sanction checks. For any domestic or foreign PEP, senior-level enhanced due diligence is compulsory, including source-of-wealth and source-of-funds analysis. Ongoing transaction monitoring is required for 12 months post-account opening; any change in UBO triggers re-screening within 24 hours. All screening results must be documented and retained for at least five years for FSS inspection.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Registry Information Center, Internet Registration Service (www.i-register.go.kr), the official Korean corporation name and registration portal.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Commercial Act and the Supreme Court Registration Business Processing Rules, a Korean company name must include a Hangul corporate form suffix equivalent to Yuhan Hoesa (limited company). The first-tier identifier may be a Hangul name, a foreign script name, or a combination; however, for search and priority purposes, the registry recognizes the Hangul spelling as the primary name, with Romanized or foreign-script names treated as secondary tags. The four-tier naming convention consists of (i) the distinctive name, (ii) the business purpose of the company, (iii) the corporate form designator (Yuhan Hoesa), and (iv) the location token of the registered office. A foreign investor may request an English trade name but must also submit an approved Hangul transliteration. Identical or deceptively similar existing names in the same registry class are barred; phonetic similarity in Hangul is assessed on the Korean orthography, not on the transliteration of a foreign trademark.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registry rejects the proposed name, the applicant or its authorized legal representative may submit a written objection application to the competent District Court Registry Office within 14 calendar days from receipt of the rejection notice. The objection must set forth the statutory grounds under Article 23(2) of the Commercial Act and explain why the name is not identical to an existing registration, not misleading, and does not violate public policy or ministerial restrictions. If the Registry still refuses, counsel may appeal by filing a registration disposition rejection appeal with the Administrative Division of the relevant court under the Administrative Litigation Act. A notarized power of attorney from the foreign investor and certified Korean translations are required; the appeal must be prosecuted in Korean and can be remedied within the 10-day statutory remedy period applicable to unincorporated acts.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or dedicated commercial mailbox is legally permissible in the Republic of Korea only if it is a fixed, physical address situated within the same district court jurisdiction that is notified to the registry as the company's registered office and where all official correspondence can be lawfully served. However, for the ISIC 7320 market research SaaS segment, the National Tax Service and domestic banks will reject a pure PO Box or non-accessible virtual address where no on-site staff, server room, or operational records exist. For corporate banking onboarding, a lease agreement covering at least 12 months for a serviced office, a workplace safety and hygiene certificate, and a utility bill in the company name are expected. For immigrant investors, the secured independent workplace requirement (Article 58 of the Immigration Act) means a virtual office will not satisfy the commercial substance test for a D-7 or D-8 visa. Consequently, the recommended approach is a high-grade coworking suite with a dedicated mail-handling service, a government-recognized building address, and a visible company sign; otherwise tax registration and bank account opening are likely to be challenged.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: The unannounced physical inspection likelihood for a market research / software company is classified as moderate-to-moderately-low (25-35% probability over the first 12 months of operation). Checklist: (1) actual compliance of the registered address with lease documents and interior signage; (2) availability of authentic accounting documents and CRM/panel data servers at the address; (3) employment status of the resident director and at least one compliance officer; (4) evidence of payroll, national pension payments, and statutory insurance enrollment for employees; (5) original VAT invoices and e-tax invoices generated from the site; (6) municipal registry inspection protocols; (7) immigration inspection if foreign director's visa requires physical business premises. The FSS Inspection Bureau may conduct risk-oriented visits after a suspended transaction report or a suspicious transaction report, and the district tax office may spot-check the business registration address without notice. The quantified risk is higher if the company files zero revenue and pays zero income tax while claiming a large, expensive office; it is sharply reduced with a 24-month lease and a dedicated mail-room service.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, enacted December 20, 1962, as amended), Articles 287-2 through 287-74 governing a Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company), together with Articles 305 and 317 on establishment registration, the Commercial Registration Act, and the relevant Enforcement Rules of the Supreme Court on Registration of Companies.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the District Court having jurisdiction over the company's registered office, especially the Seoul Central District Court Registration Division for a Seoul-headquartered company; filings are accepted through the Supreme Court's electronic commercial registry portal (i-REOS).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Establishment of a Yuhan Hoesa (Limited Liability Company), accompanied by the duly notarized Articles of Incorporation and all statutory attachment schedules.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None; no statutory minimum paid-up capital exists for a Korean Yuhan Hoesa. The subscribed capital must nevertheless be fully paid, in cash or approved in-kind property, before the establishment registration is filed. If cash is contributed, the deposit must be held in a bank account opened for the company and the deposit certificate filed with the registry. No blocked escrow account is mandated by national law; the Articles of Incorporation may impose a higher internal paid-in threshold and foreign ownership is allowed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF YUHANGHOESA (LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY). 1. CONVOCATION AND QUORUM. The inaugural board meeting of Yuhan Hoesa (the Company) was held on [date] at [time] at the proposed registered office. All duly appointed directors were present in person or by remote communication and formed a quorum under the Korean Commercial Act and the Articles of Incorporation. The chairperson declared that notice was waived and that the following matters were properly submitted for resolution. 2. RESOLUTION ON CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND ALLOTMENT. RESOLVED, that the Company subscribes, accepts, and allots the initial capital contributions set out in the Articles of Incorporation; that each founder, member, and participant shall pay the full amount of his, her, or its contribution on or before the filing date of the incorporation registration; that any non-cash contribution shall be supported by an independent appraiser's report; and that the directors are authorized to execute contribution receipts and maintain a unit ledger. 3. RESOLUTION ON BANKING AUTHORIZATION. RESOLVED, that the Company shall open and maintain corporate bank accounts with a licensed commercial bank; the Representative Director is authorized to determine signatory arrangements; any two authorized signatories, or one designated signatory as resolved by the board, may execute payment orders, payroll, foreign-currency settlements, PayPal Mass Payout funds, and Wise transfers, subject to the treasury policy and applicable AML screening; and the corporate seal and online banking certificates shall be held in binary custody except as expressly approved by the board. 4. RESOLUTION ON ADOPTION OF REGISTERED OFFICE. RESOLVED, that the Company's registered office is adopted at the address stated in the Articles of Incorporation; the office shall be a genuine physical premises suitable for cloud-based consumer polling and cross-border market-research operations; the lessor's written consent for registration is approved; and the Representative Director is authorized to file all public notices and registry submissions required to perfect the registered office. 5. RESOLUTION ON APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS. RESOLVED, that the candidates named before the meeting are hereby appointed as directors of the Company; the Representative Director is appointed as the chief executive with authority to bind the Company singly in the ordinary course of business; an auditor is appointed to serve until the first ordinary members' meeting if required by law; and all officers are authorized to initiate and lodge the establishment registration, execute all notices, and instruct law firms and certified public accountants in completing the formation. 6. ADJOURNMENT. There being no further business, the meeting was adjourned.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate name clearance and drafting of the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Supreme Court of Korea - Commercial Registration Name Search through the electronic registry portal and the District Court Registry having jurisdiction over the proposed registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a corporate name search through the court-maintained commercial registry system to verify that the proposed Yuhan Hoesa name is not identical or misleadingly similar to an existing company. Confirm the legality and availability of the business purpose, the registered office address, and the proposed governance structure. Draft the Articles of Incorporation in the official Korean legal format, setting out the corporate name, business purpose, capital, contribution units, directors, auditor, fiscal year, method of public notice, and dissolution provisions. Obtain written consent from the lessor of the registered office and collect KYC/AML information from all incorporators and directors before the notarization stage.
required_dossiers: Valid passport or national identity card of each incorporator and director
Proof of residential or business address of each incorporator
Proposed Articles of Incorporation draft
Power of attorney if signing through a representative
Notarized lessor consent for use of the registered office
KYC/AML questionnaire and ultimate beneficial owner declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name search or preliminary review is queried, propose at least three alternative corporate names and re-run the search within one business day. If the business purpose is considered ambiguous, amend the scope wording to align with ISIC 7320 and re-file before notarization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Articles and deposit of initial capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public commissioned under the Korean Notary Act, together with a licensed commercial bank authorized to issue a capital deposit certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the final Korean-language Articles of Incorporation before a notary public. The notary will verify the identity and legal capacity of every founder and director, confirm the signatures and seals, and certify the Articles. If the formation plan requires a pre-incorporation bank account, open a temporary or escrow-style account in the name of the planned company and deposit the full subscribed capital. The bank must issue a deposit certificate reflecting the exact amount of capital credited and the names of the contributors. If an in-kind contribution is used, an independent appraiser must issue a valuation report stating the market value and transferability of the contributed asset.
required_dossiers: Final Korean-language Articles of Incorporation
Notarized signatures and corporate seals of founders and directors
Capital deposit certificate from the receiving bank
In-kind contribution appraisal report, if applicable
Notarized power of attorney, if applicable
Identity documents of all persons executing before the notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary requests corrections, revise the Articles and reconvene the incorporators for re-execution within five business days. If the capital deposit certificate is disputed, obtain a corrected statement from the bank showing blocked availability of funds for the sole benefit of the company.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Application for establishment registration with the District Court and issuance of the corporate seal
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: District Court Registration Division with venue at the registered office address; electronic filing may be made through the Supreme Court commercial registry portal (i-REOS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After notarization, submit the application for registration of establishment of the Yuhan Hoesa to the district court registry. The application must contain the registered office address, capital amount, contribution units, names of directors and auditor, and the method of public notice. Attach the certified Articles, the capital deposit certificate, proof of lessor consent, identity documents, and statutory officer acceptance forms. Pay the registration tax, education tax, and court fee through the appropriate revenue system. Upon approval, the registry issues the certificate of company registration and files the corporation record. The company then creates a corporate seal, registers a sealed specimen with the court or designated seal registration office, and obtains a corporate seal certificate.
required_dossiers: Application for Registration of Establishment of a Yuhan Hoesa
Certified Articles of Incorporation
Capital deposit certificate or in-kind contribution valuation report
Minutes or written resolution of incorporation
Acceptance forms of directors and auditor
Identity cards and passports of all officers
Lease agreement and lessor consent
Registration tax and education tax payment receipts
Power of attorney, if filed by a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a supplementary order or requests corrections, provide the missing documents within seven to fourteen days of the request. If the registration is suspended, prepare a corrective filing with a sworn certificate of correction and, if necessary, demand a written statement of grounds and apply for administrative appeal within ninety days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business registration with the National Tax Service and opening of a corporate bank account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service through the HomeTax portal or the local District Tax Office, and a licensed commercial bank under Financial Services Commission supervision
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the company registration certificate and corporate seal certificate, file an application for business registration with the local tax office or through the HomeTax electronic portal. This application must be made within twenty days after incorporation or business commencement. Provide the corporate information page, the registered office lease contract, the company registration certificate, and the corporate seal certificate. The tax office will issue a Business Registration Certificate and, where relevant, a VAT registration number. After taxation documents are obtained, convene a short banking meeting using the adopted board resolution, open the corporate current account, execute the bank signature cards, and establish the payment rails, including PayPal Mass Payout and Wise, subject to bank KYC and AML approval.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Company Registration from the District Court
Corporate seal certificate and registered seal specimen
Articles of Incorporation
Lease agreement and proof of registered office
Passport or ID of the Representative Director
Board resolution authorizing bank account opening and payment rails
Business registration application form
Certificate of foreign investment or foreign-exchange declaration, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office queries the business registration, respond by submitting the certificate of company registration and the written lease consent. If the bank rejects the account application for insufficient KYC, provide apostilled passports, beneficial ownership declarations, and certified corporate resolutions; request the bank's written refusal ground and independently apply to the Financial Supervisory Service dispute channel if the refusal is arbitrary.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) would be the industrial licensing authority for physical manufacturing activities, but the certified business scope is a non-manufacturing market-research SaaS platform under ISIC 7320.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - ISIC 7320 Consumer Polling and Cross-Border Market Research Platform is a pure digital and consulting service; no manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing operating license is required.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - Ministry of Environment and the Korea Environment Corporation would administer environmental review only for physical projects; no project is subject to EIA for an office-based digital service.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - Category Exempt for the digital service model, as no construction or production facility is being established.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - zero industrial wastewater discharge, zero VOC emissions, and no hazardous waste handling arising from the business operations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for industrial operations; however, the company must still comply with general workplace safety obligations under the Occupational Safety and Health Act, including basic office fire safety verification and the lessor's fire inspection certificate for the leased office premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea (NTS) with electronic portal HomeTax at hometax.go.kr; customs export controls are administered separately by the Korea Customs Service through the UNI-PASS single-window system
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A domestic Yuhan Hoesa must obtain a 10-digit Business Registration Number, which is simultaneously its TIN and VAT identification number, from the district tax office with jurisdiction over its registered domestic place of business before commencing operations. The application is made on the official tax registration form under the Framework Act on National Taxes and the Value-Added Tax Act, accompanied by the certificate of incorporation, articles of association, director identification, board resolution, evidence of the Korean place of business, and, where relevant, foreign investor documentation. The entity is classified as a domestic corporation and cannot elect pass-through treatment. A foreign non-resident entity with no Korean place of business that is required to collect Korean VAT on electronic or digital services supplied to Korean consumers must instead complete the simplified foreign business operator registration through HomeTax under the Value-Added Tax Act and its Enforcement Decree. That registration is fully electronic, results in assignment of a 10-digit TIN/VAT number, and requires designation of a Korean tax representative where the NTS so requires. The application dossier for the simplified foreign registration must include the foreign entity's certificate of good standing, board authorization, tax representative appointment, evidence of Korean supply activities, and supporting calculation of Korean turnover.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None; Korean tax law imposes entity-level taxation on a Yuhan Hoesa as a domestic corporation under the Corporation Tax Act. There is no check-the-box pass-through election, and hybrid mismatch rules are mandatory anti-avoidance provisions rather than elective regimes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No monetary threshold for the domestic Yuhan Hoesa; VAT registration is mandatory from the commencement of any business activity. For a foreign non-resident supplier of digital or electronic services with no Korean place of business, simplified VAT registration is triggered when the annual Korean B2C supply exceeds KRW 10,000,000 in the relevant period, and registration must be completed through HomeTax by the month following the month in which the threshold is reached.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: B2B supplies must be documented through the Korean electronic tax invoice system. Electronic tax invoices issued under the e-Hometax system must be transmitted to the NTS by the day following the supply or payment date, whichever applies. There is no real-time cryptographic fiscal stamping requirement, but the NTS requires digital submission through HomeTax, supports machine-to-machine API-based transmission for approved software, and expects complete tax invoice data to be captured online. VAT returns are filed semi-annually through HomeTax, with interim prepayment returns due during the year; retail cash receipts are required for cash purchases where requested, with the receipt data transmitted to NTS.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating under Article 24 of the Value-Added Tax Act is available for exported goods and services. Goods qualify when physical export is evidenced by a validated Korea Customs Service export declaration. Services qualify when supplied to a non-resident recipient, paid for in foreign currency properly remitted through foreign exchange banking channels, and consumed or used outside Korea. For a cross-border market-research SaaS platform, the supply must be made to an overseas counterparty for a valid business purpose, and the digital service must be actually accessed or used by the non-resident counterparty outside Korea; zero-rating will not apply if the service is treated as supplied or consumed within Korea.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS electronic export declaration and acceptance number (customs export declaration / bill of entry equivalent)
Original commercial invoice and signed service contract or purchase order identifying the non-resident customer and scope of services
Bill of lading or air waybill for physical goods, or equivalent electronic evidence of service delivery for SaaS/digital services
Inward remittance certificate / foreign exchange purchase certificate issued by a licensed foreign exchange bank showing receipt and conversion of export proceeds in foreign currency
Bank statements matching the invoice value, payment dates, and remitter identity
For digital services: IP access logs, session records, platform user location data, and consumption records demonstrating actual use outside South Korea
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS and Korea Customs Service cross-check export declarations, electronically transmitted tax invoices, and foreign currency remittance records. If zero-rating is claimed but the export cannot be substantiated, the NTS reverses the claim, assesses the standard 10% VAT on the supply, and imposes statutory additional tax penalties under the Value-Added Tax Act for late payment, underdeclaration, and failure to issue or transmit electronic tax invoices. In cases involving fraud or intentional concealment, the Framework Act on National Taxes permits a ten-year retroactive assessment window, and criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act may result. The taxpayer must retain the full export documentation bundle for at least five years, and ten years where fraudulent misstatement is alleged. Fictitious or circular foreign exchange repatriation will be treated as evidence of domestic supply, triggering full VAT clawback, penalties, and possible criminal charges.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Bank of Korea (BOK) and the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) acting through the Foreign Exchange Information System operated by the Korea Customs Service and the Bank of Korea's Foreign Exchange Administration
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a liberalized foreign exchange system under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. The Korean won is fully convertible for current account transactions, including trade settlements, service fees, dividends, and royalties, subject to documentary reporting thresholds. Capital account transactions, such as foreign direct investment inbound equity subscriptions and cross-border loans, are generally permitted on a notification or declaration basis through a foreign exchange bank. There is no mandatory surrender of export proceeds, but Korean banks require exporters to report export earnings and to repatriate proceeds within a statutory period, typically within 18 months from the export date for receipt into a foreign currency account or conversion into KRW. Profit remittance hurdles are minimal for properly registered foreign-invested enterprises: a Foreign Investment Report (FIRC) issued under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act is required to evidence the initial capital injection, and subsequent dividend remittances are processed through the bank upon submission of audited financial statements and tax clearance certificates. For a market research SaaS platform receiving cross-border consumer panel survey payments, the main operational FX consideration is that inbound cross-border service receipts should be reported as export proceeds under the code for 'Service Trade - Other Business Services (Market Research)'. The lack of a dedicated capital control regime for small service receivables means the treasury operation can use standard SWIFT MT103 credits with the correct foreign exchange purpose code (e.g., code 910000 or specific service category code) without needing central bank pre-approval. Nevertheless, the bank will apply anti-money laundering screening and may request underlying contracts and invoices for amounts above the equivalent of USD 10,000. Given the regulatory framework, the entity should maintain a KRW operational account and a USD or multi-currency foreign currency account at a domestic tier-1 bank. A fintech EMI is viable only as a downstream payment collection tool supported by a licensed domestic bank settlement account, not as a primary regulated banking rail for corporate FX obligations under Korean law.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Exporters must report export earnings to the designated foreign exchange bank and repatriate the foreign currency proceeds into the exporter's foreign currency account or convert into KRW within 18 months from the date of export; the full amount must be received, and no mandatory conversion ratio is imposed, although submission of the Customs export declaration and the related service contract is required for service exports such as market research subscriptions.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational KRW Current Account
Foreign Currency Demand Deposit Account (USD) and Basic Operational KRW Account
Multi-Currency Settlement Account with Sub-Ledgers for USD and KRW
Foreign Exchange Trading Account and Corporate Treasury Clearing Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Fintech EMIs such as Wise and PayPal operate in South Korea under limited payment gateway arrangements and are not licensed as primary commercial banks under the Banking Act. They are legally barred from accepting vanilla corporate deposits or providing FX clearing services that would replace the banking system. However, the platform may use PayPal Mass Payout and Wise as peripheral collection and mass payout rails, as long as all onboarding funds are routed through a licensed domestic bank settlement account and that the EMI is integrated via open-banking APIs. The legal basis for this restriction is the Electronic Financial Transactions Act, which requires payment service providers to obtain a license from the Financial Services Commission (FSC). Since a foreign EMI typically lacks the required license, the entity should maintain a domestic corporate bank account as the settlement anchor and treat EMI collections as pre-settlement receivables subject to daily sweep into the licensed bank. Using an unlicensed EMI as the sole banking rail would constitute a compliance failure and expose the treasury structure to regulatory sanction by the FSC and the Bank of Korea.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The statutory director and the ultimate beneficial owner with 25% or more economic interest must appear physically before a designated Foreign Exchange Bank branch in South Korea to sign the corporate account opening documents and complete a face-to-face customer identification interview under the Financial Action Task Force-aligned Real Name Financial Transactions Act. Remote opening by consular proxy is not permitted when a domestic corporation is newly established with no existing banking relationship; however, after initial onboarding, signatory changes may be handled through consular notarization and couriered hard copies.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection from a foreign parent or shareholder where the funding source is a digital asset exchange or low-transparency fintech account
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a notarized capital contribution statement delivered to the foreign shareholder, certified bank statements of the remitting account for the last 12 months showing salary/investment/corporate income provenance, tax residence certificates of all shareholders, and a signed declaration confirming that the funds do not originate from crypto, gambling, or illegal telemarketing revenue; a letter of responsibility from the Korean statutory director plus a copy of the Foreign Investment Report (FIRC) after filing with the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border service revenue collected via PayPal Mass Payout or Wise lacking full payer identity screenshots and recurring volume from unfamiliar consumer panelists
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver the platform's consumer consent log, IP geographic data, the underlying survey order contract or digital terms of service, disassembled invoice PDFs matching each payout transaction, and a month-end accounts receivable reconciliation showing that all monies flowed from the survey sponsor into the licensed Korean bank; obtain an independent audit opinion on the payment data integrity before submitting to the bank's AML committee.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large round-trip payments between Korea and jurisdictions with high AML risk for market research outsourcing
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide commercial outsourcing agreements with independent contractors, transfer pricing documentation for the surveyed service fees, beneficial ownership declarations for all counterparty companies, publicly verifiable corporate registries from the counterparty country, and prior-year audited financial statements confirming the economic substance of the cross-border costs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of a low-risk industry classification ISIC 7320 when the actual activity involves data monetization, behavioral advertising, or consumer credit profiling
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit the full privacy and data processing policy, the controller-processor flow chart, the Korean PIPA compliance certification, and a legal opinion from a Korean law firm confirming that the platform does not perform consumer credit scoring or profiling that would trigger the Credit Information Act and elevate the AML risk tier.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital subscriptions must be remitted in the name of the foreign investor through an international SWIFT MT103/TT wire using the correct foreign exchange remittance code `FDI inbound equity` (code 620010). The remittance memo must state 'Application of Funds: Working capital for consumer survey platform under ISIC 7320'. After the funds arrive at the capital escrow account at the chosen domestic tier-1 bank, the entity must submit a Foreign Investment Report to obtain the FIRC, complete a foreign exchange declaration through the bank's electronic FX system, and arrange for a certified public accountant's capital verification report before funds can be released to the general operational account. Any subsequent sponsor payments for research subscriptions must be tagged as current account service receipts using the export declaration under the Korea Customs Service single-window system, referencing the underlying service agreement and commercial invoice.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operating disbursements to overseas survey panelists and research subcontractors should be processed through the licensed Korean bank's corporate internet banking platform using SWIFT MT103 for US dollar and other foreign currency payments, and through domestic KRW CD/EFT rails for local settlements. For sponsor-funded international market research campaigns exceeding USD 50,000, the treasury should prefer commercial letters of credit or documentary collection where the survey deliverables include milestone-based data deliveries and contractual acceptances; otherwise, ordinary SWIFT MT103 credits with invoice matching are acceptable for SaaS-type subscription fees. Each outbound disbursement requires a bank transaction code reflecting the purpose: code 820120 for market research services, 220010 for foreign contractors, and appropriate data processing codes.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore forward foreign exchange contracts with a domestic Korean bank supporting underlying lobby real export/service receivables
Non-deliverable forward (NDF) restrictions are governed by the Bank of Korea's guidelines; entities with genuine KRW exposure may use NDF swaps only via authorized banks for hedging, not speculating
Cross-currency swaps permitted for the conversion of inbound foreign capital contributions into KRW working capital subject to the bank's FX limit and a signed underlying commercial contract

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual members' meeting and approval of annual financial statements (Yuhan Hoesa annual corporate secretarial confirmation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate organ (members' meeting); minutes kept at the registered office and recorded in the statutory minute book; not separately filed with a regulator unless an external audit report is required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months of the fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year company ending 31 December, no later than 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the meeting and approve financial statements may subject the representative officer to administrative fines under the Commercial Act; repeated neglect of corporate formalities is treated with tax-authority and court dissolution action, including dormancy strike-off after several consecutive unfiled years

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporation Tax Return (corporate income tax) and Local Corporate Income Tax Surtax Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) through HomeTax and the competent metropolitan city/province tax office through Wetax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months from the fiscal year close; for a calendar-year company, 31 March of the immediately following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing triggers a 20% surcharge on the unpaid tax (40% for bad-faith omission), plus 0.022% daily interest per day after the statutory due date; three consecutive non-filing periods permit the NTS to close the business registration and petition the registry court for compulsory dissolution/strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: VAT preliminary and final returns (quarterly provisional filings and semi-annual final returns)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Preliminary Jan-Mar return due 25 April; preliminary Jul-Sep return due 25 October; final Jan-Jun return due 25 July; final Jul-Dec return due 25 January
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late VAT returns are charged additional tax at 0.75% of the unpaid VAT per day for the first 30 days and 1.5% per day thereafter, with registration closure and criminal referral for chronic failure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer withholding returns and annual wage and business payment statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly withholding tax payment and return due on the 10th day of the following month; annual employee wage statements for the prior calendar year due by the last business day of February
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to remit withheld taxes exposes the company to late-payment surcharge (0.022% per day) and a withholding violation penalty of up to 20% of the unreported amount; chronic defaults can lead to business registration cancellation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foreign-Invested Enterprise Report (FDI annual report and UBO confirmation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through KOTRA, with record filing to the Bank of Korea / foreign-exchange reporting system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days from the fiscal year-end; for a 31 December fiscal year, no later than 30 January
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file accurately imposes administrative fines under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, carries a compliance black-mark that can block tax treaty benefits and dividend remittances, but by itself does not administratively strike off the entity

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Event-driven commercial registry update and beneficial ownership transfer filing (annual maintenance confirmation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korean registry court (Commercial Registry) and the National Tax Service for beneficial-ownership tax records
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Registered changes of directors, members' quotas, quotas pledge, or registered agents must be recorded within two weeks of the triggering event; annual renewal is not separately required in Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late registration subjects the company to court registry surcharges and a refusal to recognize corporate changes against third parties; failure to maintain an accurate register supports tax evasion penalties and judicial dissolution in aggravated cases

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Korean Act on External Audit of Stock Companies and its Enforcement Decree, a Yuhan Hoesa limited liability company must retain an independent Korean certified public accountant (CPA) who is registered with the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants whenever the company is not a small company exemption and, as of the immediately preceding fiscal year-end, (i) total assets equal or exceed KRW 10 billion (approx. USD 7.45 million); (ii) the company is a subsidiary whose parent is required to prepare consolidated K-IFRS financial statements; (iii) the company is designated as a public-interest or other audit-mandated entity by statute; or (iv) a special law (financial licensing, cross-border payment institutional status, or government-funded research) imposes an audit. For small- and medium-sized unlisted service companies (including this consumer panel SaaS), the ordinary mandatory threshold is therefore total assets of KRW 10 billion or more; below that, certified audit is elective rather than legally required unless foreign-investment or lender covenants impose it.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) for listed and large-audit companies; Korea's statutory accounting standards (Korean GAAP) for other companies required to audit; and the Korean SME/Micro-entity accounting standards for small non-audited companies. All financial statements are expressed in KRW and filed under the same accounting framework used for the corporate tax return.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not impose an annual standalone UBO report on a domestic Yuhan Hoesa. The statutory protocol is maintenance of an up-to-date member register and identity records, annual confirmation of ultimate individual shareholders inside the Foreign-Invested Enterprise Annual Report, and event-driven reporting within 30 days for any cross-border transfer of quotas or UBO change under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act / Foreign Investment Promotion Act. Domestic quota transfers are perfected by member meeting approval, amendment of the articles, and commercial registry registration within two weeks; the tax authorities must be notified of the gain/loss, and the new member becomes effective for corporate income tax from the transfer date.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 - USD 2,000 per year for a registered-office address and corporate agent with compliance notification service
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 - USD 12,000 for a small/mid-size Yuhan Hoesa using Korean GAAP; larger K-IFRS or group audit engagements may start at USD 25,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 22% national top marginal corporate income tax rate for taxable income above KRW 300 billion, plus 10% local income tax surtax on national corporate tax producing a 24.2% top combined statutory burden; lower brackets are 9% up to KRW 200 million, 19% above KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion, and 21% above KRW 20 billion to KRW 300 billion
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualified foreign-invested enterprises may claim corporate income tax holiday/reduction under the Tax Incentive Limitation Law, including 100% exemption for the first three years and 50% reduction for the following two years for eligible foreign direct investment in Free Economic Zones; high-technology inbound investment can obtain further reductions; R&D expenditures generate incremental corporate tax credits up to 25%; certain capital investment in productivity/security facilities is creditable; patent box-type regimes are not separately codified but IP-derived income can be sheltered through R&D credits and transfer-pricing planning if substance is established

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Korean Corporate Income Tax Return (Corporate Tax Base and Tax Computation Return) filed electronically through the National Tax Service HomeTax portal (www.hometax.go.kr); foreign-transaction supporting schedules and OECD transfer-pricing documentation are attached
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; a half-year provisional corporate income tax return and payment are required within two months after the end of the first six months, followed by the final annual return and settlement
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The final corporate income tax return must be filed within three months after the end of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year Yuhan Hoesa the statutory deadline is 31 March unless an approved extension applies

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Taxpayer Identity and Filing Period
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate registration number, legal name, head office address, representative director, fiscal year-end, Korean Standard Industrial Classification code, paid-in capital, shareholder registry, and consolidated/individual return indicator.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose the ultimate non-resident shareholder's jurisdiction of tax residence, percent shareholding, and any election to treat the Korean LLC as a domestic corporation; if the foreign shareholder claims treaty capacity, attach a Tax Residency Certificate and note that the Korean entity reports worldwide corporate income regardless of where foreign owners are domiciled.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Gross Revenue and Business Income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross sales and operating income from consumer panel survey subscriptions, market research SaaS contracts, data licensing, panelist management fees, advertising, and cross-border payout commissions settled through PayPal/Wise or any other payment rail.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Recognize revenue on an accrual basis when the survey or research service is performed; convert foreign-currency settlements into KRW using the Bank of Korea base rate at the accrual date; list all controlled transactions with foreign related parties separately so that the tax return can be reconciled with the Local File; revenue earned from overseas respondents remains part of the Korean taxable base because the Korean LLC is the enterprise that owns the platform and performs the core activities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Non-Taxable Income and Exempt Items
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Capital contributions received without consideration, certain government grants legally classified as nontaxable, dividend income qualifying for the dividends-received deduction, and legal reserve additions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not classify platform grant money, panelist advances, or customer deposits as non-taxable; if treaty protection is asserted over a particular revenue stream, attach the tax treaty return-position memorandum and identify the article relied on; the National Tax Service will recharacterize non-arm's-length capital injections into taxable income if the transaction lacks commercial substance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Deductible Expenses and Non-Deductible Items
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Ordinary and necessary expenses including compensation, cloud hosting, data licensing, panelist rewards, marketing, rent, depreciation, legal, accounting, and consulting fees, together with ad-hoc non-deductible adjustments such as entertainment limits and fines.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany service fees, management fees, royalties, and data-processing charges paid to foreign affiliates are deductible only if supported by written contracts, actual invoices, evident performance of services, benefit created for the Korean LLC, and OECD-compliant arm's-length pricing; any such payment to a non-resident is subject to Korean withholding tax remitted by the 10th day of the following month, and failure to withhold will cause the expense to be denied and expose the company to penalty tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Tax Base Computation Before Loss Carryforward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of gross taxable income after adding non-deductible expenses, subtracting non-taxable income and income exemptions, and applying prior-year tax return adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the Korean LLC is the overseas extension of a foreign market-research group, all Korean operational profits must be allocated to this return; no profit may be shifted to a foreign parent solely through the payment of artificial platform-license fees unless the foreign entity owns income-generating intangibles and performs active decision-making; attach an economic substance summary proving that the Korean entity controls the consumer panel platform, contracts with customers, manages risk, and employs the personnel who generate revenue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduction of eligible prior-year tax losses within the statutory carryforward period of five fiscal years, subject to traceable continuity of business.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the ownership continuity history because a change of 50% or more in foreign shareholding combined with a change of business may trigger anti-loss-trafficking rules and deny the deduction; if the loss shield is restructured through new non-resident investors, expect the National Tax Service to audit whether the loss was genuine and whether continuity was maintained.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 - Transfer-Pricing Adjustments and Related-Party Transaction Schedule
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Line-by-line add-backs, adjustments, and recharacterization of controlled transactions with foreign related parties to reflect arm's-length conditions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For each intercompany royalty, marketing fee, survey panel data fee, interest charge, and SaaS license fee, attach the transfer-pricing method selected (CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, or Profit Split), the benchmarking study, and the contractual allocation of risks; failure to maintain and file contemporaneous documentation upon request can result in penalty taxes and adjustment of the Korean taxable base upward.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Application of statutory tax holidays, foreign investment incentives, free economic zone reductions, and other tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Substantiate that qualifying business activities actually occur in Korea: local employment, physical premises, board meetings, operational decisions, and bank accounts; if the Yuhan Hoesa is used only as a shell to receive dividends, royalties, or passive income, the incentive will be clawed back with penalty taxes and the beneficial-ownership claim under a tax treaty will be denied.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the progressive statutory rates to the taxable base, compute national corporate income tax, and add the 10% local income tax surtax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure that dividends or profits remitted abroad are sourced from after-tax retained earnings only; the tax computation must include the full Korean tax charge before any foreign tax credit claimed for taxes paid in the non-resident owner's home jurisdiction, and the foreign tax credit limitation must be calculated per-country and per-income-class to avoid double-dipping.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credits, R&D credits, job creation credits, preliminary return payments, wage tax withholdings, and any creditable non-resident withholding taxes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: To claim credit for foreign withholding tax, attach the foreign tax return or withholding certificate showing the exact amount, the income to which it relates, and the rate charged; treaty withholding rates must not be claimed unilaterally without the HomeTax-approved treaty application number and the foreign Tax Residency Certificate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 11 - Non-Resident Withholding and Remittance Summary
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate schedule of dividends, interest, royalties, and service fees paid or credited to non-residents, including the identity of each payee, country of residence, income code, gross amount, statutory withholding rate, treaty rate applied, and withheld tax remitted.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This box is the centralized compliance point for outbound payments; each non-resident recipient must provide a Tax Residency Certificate, beneficial ownership declaration, and limitation-on-benefits/principal-purpose-test statement; if the approved treaty rate is not obtained before payment, the payer must withhold at the 22% effective statutory rate and the over-withheld amount may only be recovered by the non-resident through a tax refund claim within three years.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 12 - Tax Payable, Settlement, and Refund
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final amount of corporate income tax payable after applying preliminary payments, credits, and withholding; computation of installment amounts, late payment surcharges, and refunds.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payment must be made by the statutory deadline in KRW through HomeTax; any repatriation of profit in the same tax period must be disclosed to demonstrate that dividends were declared from real accumulated earnings and not thinly capitalized loans; mismatch between cash repatriated and Box 9 after-tax profit is a principal audit trigger.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file or a false return triggers additional taxes under the Framework Act on National and Local Taxes: 20% of unpaid tax for non-filing, 10% of understated amount for ordinary under-reporting, and 40% of understated amount for fraudulent under-reporting; late payment accrues daily surcharges at the statutory rate; criminal referral is mandatory for intentional tax evasion under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, with imprisonment up to five years or a fine up to three times the evaded tax; directors can be made secondarily liable for unpaid corporate tax and may be placed on the public tax-delinquent blacklist and subjected to exit bans.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% national withholding tax on outbound dividends plus a 2% additional local income tax surtax, producing an effective statutory rate of 22%; the rate may be reduced under a bilateral income tax treaty
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke Double Tax Treaty relief, the non-resident shareholder must obtain a Tax Residency Certificate from the competent tax authority of its jurisdiction, prove beneficial ownership by holding substantive equity, financial, and management records, and demonstrate that the arrangement is not designed to obtain treaty benefits under the Principal Purpose Test; before each dividend remittance, the Korean payer must submit the HomeTax treaty application and withholding exemption/abatement form, attach the Tax Residency Certificate, shareholder register, limited-benefits/LOB declaration, and confirm that the shareholder has no Korean permanent establishment; once approved, the payer applies the treaty rate at source; if the application is made after tax was withheld, the non-resident must file a refund claim with the Korean district tax office within three years of the statutory withholding payment date
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates for outbound royalties and intercompany interest are 20% national withholding tax plus 2% local income tax surtax, a 22% effective charge; under most Korean bilateral tax treaties the reduced rates are 10%-15% for royalties and 0%-15% for interest depending on the treaty partner and type of payment, but treaty relief is available only with current Tax Residency Certificates, beneficial ownership evidence, no Korean permanent establishment attributable to the income, and satisfaction of the Principal Purpose Test; interest paid on thinly capitalized loans from controlling foreign shareholders may be disallowed as a deduction and recharacterized as a dividend.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Contemporaneous Local File documentation is mandatory for a Korean company when cross-border controlled transactions with a foreign related party exceed KRW 5 billion in the fiscal year; Master File documentation is required where the multinational group's consolidated revenue exceeds KRW 100 billion, and Country-by-Country reporting applies to groups with consolidated group revenue of at least KRW 100 billion; when a lower transaction threshold exists for a specific industry or tax-haven jurisdiction, separate reporting schedules govern.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Republic of Korea is not an Economic Substance Regulations jurisdiction of the Gulf model, but its substance-over-form jurisprudence, permanent establishment rules, treaty beneficial-ownership requirements, and general anti-avoidance doctrines require a Korean entity to demonstrate real offices, employees, bank accounts, board minutes, risk management, and customer contracting activity; for a consumer panel survey SaaS platform, the Core Income-Generating Activities must be performed in Korea or attributed to a Korean permanent establishment, including platform development, data hosting, client contracting, panelist management, invoicing, and after-sales support, otherwise the National Tax Service will disregard the Korean entity or deny treaty and incentive benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally omitting consumer panel survey SaaS revenue, concealing PayPal/Wise settlement accounts, issuing false invoices, and failing to report KRW attributable to cross-border market research services in order to reduce the Korean corporate income tax base.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 3 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, fraudulent evasion is punishable by imprisonment for up to five years or a fine of up to three times the tax evaded; the National Tax Service also imposes a 40% negligence penalty on the fraudulently under-reported amount and can publish the company as a tax evader.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil may be pierced when the entity is a sham or when directors intentionally cause the company to defraud tax authorities; directors are jointly and severally liable for corporate tax under Article 39 of the National Tax Collection Act if they actively manipulate funds, must make civil restitution of diverted corporate assets, face exit bans and blacklisting by the tax administration, and remain exposed to criminal imprisonment for tax fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Abuse and Profit Stripping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying excessive royalties, management fees, marketing support fees, or intercompany interest to foreign related parties for consumer panel data and platform intangibles without economic substance, while the Korean Yuhan Hoesa performs all revenue-generating functions, bears risk, and employs all staff, thereby shifting Korean taxable profits abroad.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Framework Act on International Tax Adjustment requires arm's-length pricing and permits the National Tax Service to adjust the tax base, impose a secondary adjustment declaring the excess remittance as a deemed dividend, and assess penalty taxes for failure to submit transfer-pricing documentation or for filing a return inconsistent with the arm's-length result.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who execute sham intercompany agreements or certify false transfer-pricing studies can be held civilly liable for the resulting tax and penalties, be required to restore the company's lost assets, be named on the tax-delinquent blacklist, be restricted from international departure, and may face imprisonment for willful preparation of false tax filings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Economic Substance Abuse / Treaty Shopping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the Korean LLC only as a shell to receive outbound dividends, royalties, or foreign investment tax holidays while actual ownership decisions, customer contracts, data processing, and risk management are conducted by non-resident persons abroad, with no local employees, office, bank account transparency, or business activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The National Tax Service can disregard the shell entity under substance-over-form principles, deny treaty reductions under the General Anti-Avoidance Rule and the Principal Purpose Test, revoke foreign-investment tax incentives retroactively, assess corporate income tax on undistributed profits, and apply the 40% fraudulent-return penalty where the shell structure was knowingly concealed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors will be personally liable for unpaid tax and interest where the corporate form has been abused to evade tax, may be ordered by Korean courts to pay restitution to the tax authority or injured creditors, are exposed to exit bans and public blacklisting, and can be criminally prosecuted under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act for deliberate use of a no-substance conduit, carrying up to five years' imprisonment.
